# Resources

## Purpose

Knowledge and reference materials on topics of interest that may be useful in the future. A resource answers the question “What am I studying or saving for reuse?”

## Include

- Notes from books, articles, lectures, and courses for general study of a topic.
- Reference guides, instructions, templates, collections, and examples for reuse.
- Ideas and observations not yet connected to an active project or an ongoing responsibility.
- Examples: “Programming” with notes on approaches, “Photography” with shooting techniques, “History” with study notes, and “Recipes” with a collection of dishes.

## Exclude

- Working materials created for a specific active outcome — the Projects folder (`1 Projects`).
- Documents and records used to manage an ongoing responsibility — the Areas folder (`2 Areas`).
- Outdated collections and materials on topics no longer needed for current work or study — the Archives folder (`4 Archives`).

## Placement guidelines

Group resources by topic when helpful. Each subfolder's description should state its subject and scope so that related topics can be distinguished.

General-purpose material stays here even when a project links to it. If a note describes specific decisions or actions for just one project, it belongs in that project. Duplicating files is not required; a link is enough.
